items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: Leith Stevens was the CBS conductor. And they featured Bunny.

ctx.x: Yeah. I mean how did your thought process go to try to figure out what it was?

You know I really didn’t try to intellectualize it at all, I just knew I heard that sound and it carried so much emotion and expression and everything that it just flipped me out. And then the next big guy was this guy Bunny Berigan. He was actually, you know Louis once said, when asked who his favorite trumpet player was, “My boy is Bunny.” And I know why, because Bunny was actually an outgrowth of Louis. Bunny used to say when you go on the road all you need is a toothbrush and some Louis records. Bunny was…

I did, but as a writer. He wrote for Down Beat in the early stages, and he became the Record of the Month producer for Reader’s Digest. And when we were kids, literally high school kids, we had a little band, he and I and a couple of others. And we played Saturday night at Morton’s Corners in a place where dances were half round and half square. We were the round thank God. And the job started at a certain time, but I would not leave my house until Bunny’s show was over. Then I would go to the job.
